title: More GBA game ideas built with Astra
author: HugoDzz
selftext: I'm really blown away by that model! It can write better C than me (I'm a Rust guy but I do have some grasp over C) and use my sprite API on its own for everything assets.

comments.author: HugoDzz
comments.body:
https://preview.redd.it/pa860dcg04ph1.jpeg?width=2400&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=e8eca492c67038bcf69199c3c3c9627b30397322

These are real ROMs running on my GBA AGS-001! I’ve put my process and prompts in a [write-up here](https://www.spritefusion.com/blog/making-a-game-boy-advance-game-with-gpt-6-astra).

comments.author: CoffeeAddictus
comments.body: Looks pretty cool! How long did it take to get right?

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body: Surprisingly short! \*Most\* of the time were spent on back and forth refining the game-feel. Assets API was hooked to Codex, code is overall solid (though I have asked small architecture tweaks).

replies.author: BUTTHOLE_MONSTER
replies.body: Could you tell me more about what you do with assets? I am just grabbing actual asset packs and using those but it sounds like you have a system?

comments.body: I wonder for Pokémon fangames what this means. Inherently can be as big of a game as you want it to be.

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body: Yep, gen 3 Pokémon games are my favorite by far, now it's fairly easy to make some sprites fitting the art direction of these times.

comments.author: Exc0re
comments.body: I create game boy games with gb studio. So it seems that i can make those now completely with ai?

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body: I also use GBStudio, but this one is made with Codex with GPT-6 and Sprite Fusion for all assets.

comments.author: anon999387
comments.body: If the market knows how easy games are going to be to make, I wonder how that will affect prices.  Would you pay $30 for a game if you knew AI made it in 2 days?

replies.author: HugoDzz
replies.body:
That’s a good question. My guess is if you propose something great people will be willing to pay.

I think the labor value is kind of a lie, if one dig a whole hole with a spoon, that’s hard and long but doesn’t create any value.

And opposite: Picasso signing a sketch instantly creates a lot of value.

So here the AI did executed things but I still steered it a lot, which, I think, creates some value.

replies.author: Kosh_Ascadian
replies.body:
Game prices have been relatively detached from the time/effort to make them for ages. Smaller indie titles especially. You have projects that took 2 months on sale for the same price as things that took 6 years. And both of them are usually relatively cheap compared to the work already. 

So I don't think game prices will lower a whole lot.

Expectations on quality, amount of content, bug freedom, developer response to feedback, continuance of support longterm etc will all presumably go up a lot tho. And the percentage of games getting any sales will keep going down.
